steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium, indirect heat and lightly oil the grate.
Season pork tenderloins with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Place 1/2 of the BBQ sauce into a small bowl for basting; set aside remaining BBQ sauce for serving.
Cook pork on the preheated grill over indirect heat for 30 minutes.

Brush pork with BBQ sauce, turn, and brush again, using all sauce in the small bowl. Continue cooking until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 15 more minutes. Let pork rest for 10 minutes.
Slice pork and serve with reserved BBQ sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This grilled pork tenderloin is simple seasoned and basted with BBQ sauce while it cooks on the grill for tender, flavorful, juicy pork every time.

review.reviewBody: Indirect on the grill means to put the meat in the center of the grill and, on a gas grill, turn off the burners directly under the meat. On a charcoal grill place the charcoal on the sides of the grill so none of the charcoal is directly under the meat. Weber grills usually come with an accessory that will keep the charcoal in place or maybe a trip to the hardware store for an accessory. This is also a good way to cook chicken.

Quick and easy recipe. Very tasty. I would add that the secret to a moist thick cut of pork, which a loin is, is to cook it slowly so it doesn't dry out. I heat my grill until it's popping hot - 600 to 700 degrees F. After oiling the grates place the seasoned loin over the direct heat for one minute to sear that side of the loin. After one minute turn the loin to sear the other side, baste with bbq sauce and turn off one burner and lower the other 1 or 2 burners to the lowest setting to get the bbq down to 325 - 350 degrees and continue cooking over indirect heat. After about 15 minutes turn the loin again and baste with bbq sauce. Continue approx another 15 minutes. A meat thermometer is recommended to establish an internal temperature of 145 degrees. Remove the loin at 145 and tent with foil at least 10 minutes. Slice diagonally. I guarantee the pork will be moist, tasty and very enjoyable.

I could not cook this on indirect heat, as I was cooking on a Weber Baby Q. I heated the grill to medium high and seared the meat on both sides. I cooked it on the far side of the grill as far away from the flame as possible with medium heat for 30 minutes. I basted periodically with lots of Sweet Baby Ray's. BBQ sauce. We loved it. 
Served with potato salad, kale salad, and corn on the cob.

Absolutely the best pork loin I've ever made. Other than searing it for a minute on each side before cooking it over indirect heat, followed cooking instructions exactly. Instead of barbeque sauce, used FISCHER & WIESER's Charred Pineapple Bourbon Sauce. It was amazing!!!

I wanted to say thanks for this great recipe. I did it on a T-Fal Opti-Grill. It came out great. I had to wrap the pork in foil, and was worried that it would steam the meat, and make it tough. Didn't happen. Came out perfect. 

Would definitely advise monitoring pork with a meat thermometer. I think that's what helped me!

Coated in mango, coconut dipping sauce. Amazing.

Cooked indirect with a little pecan wood chips in the chip box sitting directly on the coals. No need to put a clock on this. I removed at 138 degrees internal and let it rest to 142 degrees internal. Wonderful flavor with the Blackberry/Chipotle BBQ sauce I had on hand. If you have a Weber grill, almost impossible to not grill like a pro.

I used fresh garlic in addition to the other seasonings and it was great. I also did a quick salt/sugar brine before seasoning, I prefer soak loins in a brine before grilling because it seems to keep it more moist and has a better texture. For the BBQ sauce I made my own, brown sugar habanero. I brushed some on shortly before removing from the grill. To keep this from being over direct heat you put your charcoal on one side of the grill. You place the loin over the coals with the lid shut until it's got a good char, do both sides. Then finishing cooking on the side where there are no coals and shut the lid. Cooking about 5 minutes on each side for a 1lb roast or until 160 degrees inside. Times will vary on how good of a fire you've got going. I hope this helps.

Grilled Pork Tenderloin Haiku: "DANG, this was so good. And as easy as can be. Marinated mine." I treated the garlic powder, S&P like a dry rub, then poured the BBQ sauce into and over the pork tenderloin in a large ziploc bag for 4 hrs. Grilled as instructed and was rewarded w/ a crazy tender, moist, perfect hunk o' pork.

SO good! I broiled it in the oven and added onion powder and chili powder as well as minced garlic rather than garlic powder and I was floored with how freaking delicious it was. 10/10 would make again.

45 minutes on a charcoal grill was perfect! I made a pile of coals on one side of the grill. I started by putting the tenderloin over the flame for about 3-5 minutes for each of the four sides (about 15 minutes). I then put the tenderloin just to the side of the flame for ten minutes each side (only the 2 large sides), then for another 5 on each side with the BBQ sauce (I used sweet baby rays). I let it rest for 10 minutes under foil, while I made butter parmesan noodles and butter and garlic sautéed broccoli. This was the best tenderloin I have made to date!! Definitely will make this again!!

Made this for dinner last night for 10 people; so simple and delicious. Juiciest tenderloin we've ever had! I rubbed it with olive oil, sprinkled liberally with garlic powder, salt and pepper, and let it sit it fridge for about 30 minutes. I grilled it with just dry ingredients for 20 minutes on indirect heat. Then placed it directly on flame brushed with bbq sauce, flipping periodically and repeating on each side until it came to temperature. Served it with grilled pineapple and sweet peppers charred on the grill. I will always do it this way from now on... SO good!
I’ve been making it. I’ve been making this for years. It’s my go to pork tenderloin recipe amazingly easy.
Great recipe. Added 1/2 tsp of onion may someone recommended. Took 20 minutes on the grill on indirect heat to get to 155 degrees so watch the time. Moist and very tasty! Definitely a keeper!
I added 1/2 teaspoon onion powder and a little extra garlic. Came out really good.
This was amazing! I would highly recommend you have an instant-read thermometer to check the Tenderloin. We will definitely make this again.

What a great recipe and so easy. I have made it several times and it has a warm pink center which helps retain the moistness. Everyone raves over it. This last time I baked it in the oven at 325 as it was too cold to grill. Cooked for the same length of time at 325 degrees and it turned out great.
I was out of gas so I had to use my smokeless electric grill. The result was less than I expected but still good. I will try this again using my outdoor grill.
